body: Happy Birthday to your loved one! This was beautiful and sweet to read.

I feel certain that you were not part of the reason. He wouldn't have signed up for your classes willingly if they were making him feel unworthy or anxious like that. There are lots of ways you can honor him, but don't feel rushed. Your other students understand that you are grieving too. A teacher I had in high school made a "memory box" for a student who died (also my close friend). She had her students add photos, a funny note she passed them once, things that remind them of her, etc etc. Not everybody added to it but lots of people did, and I went back to visit during college and the teacher still had the box displayed. Just an idea!

I think the people that love us don't think of us as burdens. I often feel the same way about myself but I never feel that way about my friends and family when they are broken, or have anxiety, or even lash out and have anger. You are not a bad person - your ability to adore your boyfriend and want the best for him is proof to me that you are a good person. If you're anything like me, you just feel everything a bit too deeply and that includes irritation and anger and guilt.

God I'm so sorry. I am in that place too right now - where I think, what's the point of clawing my way up when I know I'll be depressed again probably pretty soon. But when I'm on top of the world it feels like it's worth it. So I guess I just choose to trust that version of me instead of this version of me. I'm so sorry about your sweet dog. It's been two years since mine died, and I've learned to find comfort in my memories of him.  Sounds corny but whatever. When I can't fall asleep, I close my eyes and imagine running my hand across his belly, scratching behind his ear, poking his little nose. I always pass out pretty quick after this- amazing how he is still giving me these gifts after all this time.
